title: Getting customers, keeping customers, repeat sales

sections.skill: Track retention and build repeat sales

questions.prompt: What is retention?

choices.text: The number of new ads placed each month
The share of customers who come back

questions.correct_answer: The share of customers who come back
questions.intro: Getting a new customer usually costs more effort than keeping one. RETENTION is the share of customers who come back. REPEAT SALES come from good products, reliable service, easy reordering, and staying in touch with permission (an email list, a loyalty card, a reminder when a refill is due). A business that loses most customers after one purchase must keep finding new ones. Track how many customers buy again within a set period, such as 90 days.

questions.prompt: Why do people return to the barber?

choices.text: Prices change a lot at every single visit
Good cuts, easy booking and being remembered

questions.correct_answer: Good cuts, easy booking and being remembered
questions.intro: Many people return to the same barber for years because the cut is good, booking is easy, and the barber remembers them. The barber does not need to find a brand-new customer every time. Each happy, returning customer saves the effort and cost of attracting someone new, and may bring friends. Over years, that loyalty adds up to a steady business.
